images.name: Expanding dual knob
images.mechanism: The connector ITSELF grows concentrically into a flat dual concentric knob centered on its original cable anchor, straddling the node's left edge. Rest: tiny connector, faint tiny amber arc. Open: central gray disk with a pointer indicates base position; a concentric amber arc outside it indicates modulation range, with two small endpoint handles and an arrowhead for direction. Cable stays connected to original center, with its last segment hidden behind the expanded disk. Expanded disk radius about one fifth node width; preview stays in place, does not shrink. Adjust: cursor pulls one outer arc endpoint inward, making the amber range clearly shorter, while inner disk pointer and node stay unchanged. Direction arrow remains visible. No extra rail. This is a software modulation knob, never a physical knob.

images.name: Cable range rail
images.mechanism: Rest: tiny connector. Open: a short horizontal range rail unfolds LEFTWARD along the final straight part of the incoming cable, ending at the stationary connector. The original cable remains a thin baseline. A gray position diamond sits midway along this short rail; an amber segment with TWO endpoint handles shows the modulation interval around it; a small arrowhead on the interval shows direction. No surrounding panel or pill. Adjust: cursor drags the right endpoint inward toward the fixed position diamond so the interval visibly shortens. Connector, node and diamond stay fixed. Clearly distinguish the endpoint circles from the diamond.

images.name: Socket fan
images.mechanism: Rest: tiny connector. Open: a thin SEMICIRCULAR fan opens LEFT of the node from the stationary socket as pivot. It resembles a flat pencil-drawn angle control, not a circular knob and not a popup. A gray radial spoke sets base position; two thin boundary rays with small handles delimit a pale amber sector for range. A curved arrow inside the sector indicates direction. Node and preview untouched. Cable still meets the fixed socket pivot. Adjust: cursor brings one boundary ray toward the other, making the sector visibly narrower; gray base spoke remains in place. Only the fan is new; no inner knob disk.

images.name: Picture handles
images.mechanism: Rest: tiny connector. Open: connector remains small; it reveals a direct-manipulation overlay ON the existing rings preview, without any external panel. A gray center crosshair marks the base position; two concentric thin amber limit circles with small handles mark inner and outer modulation limits, and one radial arrow indicates outward direction. These thin control outlines are clearly distinguishable from the thick gray picture rings. A fine dotted leader from the connector associates it with the overlay. Adjust: cursor drags the OUTER amber circle handle inward, reducing the gap between the two limit circles while the center crosshair, connector, picture and node remain fixed. This option is specifically for a spatial/radial parameter, not a universal scalar control.

images.name: Multiple modulators — retained draft
images.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. NEW low fidelity interaction concept, landscape 3:2 on uniform white paper. Gray pencil sketch, amber modulation cables and accents only. No glow, no waveform, no hardware, no sidebar, no extra graph. Three columns compare alternatives for MULTIPLE LFO SOURCES feeding ONE parameter connector on the LEFT boundary of a picture node. Each column has two small source nodes to the left, each containing a single amber dot, labeled A and B. Their two amber cables converge into ONE enlarged circular socket attached to the left edge of a large rounded rectangular node containing rough concentric gray rings. Both sources must remain visibly present and independently identifiable. This is a design exploration, not a implemented UI. Columns are labeled "Add", "Multiply", "FM". Add: enlarged socket is a circle containing a small plus; A and B both enter it, small separate amber arc segments around the socket represent per-source amounts. Multiply: same geometry but socket contains a multiplication sign; distinct per-source arc segments. FM: the connector grows a small joined capsule left of the node with mini circles labeled B then A and a directional arrow from B into A, followed by arrow to the node socket. This explicitly means B changes A's speed, and A drives the parameter, not a sum. Put a tiny handwritten "speed" over the B to A arrow. Preserve picture dominance, compact attachment. Near lower part of FM column add a simple arrow cursor on source B's arc handle to suggest per-source depth adjustment. All sources feed the SAME parameter, never create two separate parameter tabs. No unrelated nodes. No footer or title. Allowed text only: Add, Multiply, FM, A, B, speed. Favor clear topology over decorative detail.

images.name: Multiple modulators
images.prompt: Edit this study. Preserve its three columns, all node locations, labels, topology, icons and rough low-fidelity sketch. Change ONLY the treatment to uniform pure white paper background, dark gray pencil lines, flat muted amber cables and arcs. Remove ALL dark shading, ALL halos and ALL glow. White background everywhere including margins. No gradients. Preserve the words Add, Multiply, FM, A, B, speed. The FM capsule should visibly touch the receiver left edge so it reads as attached.
